questions.title: Conditional quantile regression: derivation, implementation, reproduction and inference
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted known-result research analysis of fixed-dimensional linear conditional quantile regression for independent observations. The conditional error density may depend on the regressors. In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, define the estimand and pinball objective, give explicit identification, moment, design and local-density conditions, justify consistency, derive the local nonsmooth objective expansion and asymptotic distribution, and justify a feasible density-weighted sandwich covariance with explicit bandwidth conditions. Distinguish the covariance of the coefficient estimator from the covariance of its square-root-n limit. A differentiable sample-score argument without justification is insufficient. Reproduce the pinned statsmodels quantile-regression tests and Engel-data fit, report their actual results, and explain the scope of the library covariance calculations rather than assuming a robust label proves arbitrary heteroskedastic validity. Implement the public estimator interface in Python using disclosed numerical or statistical libraries as appropriate. Use exploratory numerical work and simulation to challenge the theory and implementation, including the optimization objective, conditional-quantile centering and covariance normalization. Independently review stable exact theory and source; then freeze and execute confirmation in at least two nondegenerate designs, including constant and regressor-dependent error scales, each with at least 1000 independent datasets and coverage Monte Carlo standard error at most 0.01. Assess coefficient bias, nominal 95 percent interval coverage, estimated-versus-empirical covariance and numerical failures; freeze seeds, criteria, precision and stopping before outcomes are observed. Report all unmet criteria and remaining gaps. The final report must bind actual source reproduction, current theory and code, independent review and confirmatory evidence. This is not scalar unconditional quantile estimation, blind rediscovery, a novelty claim, new R execution or reproduction of all original-paper experiments. Formalization is not required.

source.primary_authority: Koenker and Bassett (1978), Regression Quantiles, Econometrica 46(1), 33-50, DOI 10.2307/1913643; Knight (1998), Limiting Distributions for L1 Regression Estimators under General Conditions, Annals of Statistics 26(2), 755-770, DOI 10.1214/aos/1028144858. The task's random-design heteroskedastic extension requires its own stated conditions and argument. Reproduction uses unmodified statsmodels 0.14.6 at commit 40e6a84d26ac74623c6b94b718f0987ef0351c53, not historical author experiments.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.shape: Finite n-by-p matrix, n>=40, 1<=p<=6 and n>p.
request_fields.edge_cases: Any intended intercept is an explicit supplied column of ones. Evaluated designs are full rank and numerically well-conditioned.
request_fields.meaning: Regressors for the linear conditional quantile; do not add a hidden intercept or regularization.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.edge_cases: Responses may be negative; this is not a conditional mean or a sorted univariate quantile problem.

request_fields.name: quantile
request_fields.edge_cases: Both median and asymmetric quantiles are valid; do not replace the requested level with 0.5.

request_fields.name: bandwidth
request_fields.edge_cases: Use the supplied bandwidth unchanged; evaluated fits have a nonsingular density-weighted sample Jacobian.
request_fields.meaning: Bandwidth for a standard-normal kernel applied to fitted residuals when estimating the density-weighted regression Jacobian.

response_fields.name: coefficients
response_fields.edge_cases: Any numerically resolved minimizer is admissible if multiple solutions exist; no optimizer or tie-breaking algorithm is prescribed.
response_fields.meaning: Minimizer of the mean pinball loss at the requested conditional quantile.

response_fields.name: mean_pinball_loss
response_fields.edge_cases: Evaluate the objective at the returned coefficients using every observation.
response_fields.meaning: Average of u*(quantile-indicator(u<0)) for residual u=y-x*coefficients.
response_fields.normalization: Divide the loss sum by n exactly once.

response_fields.name: density_jacobian
response_fields.shape: Finite symmetric p-by-p matrix on convergence.
response_fields.edge_cases: Weight each x_i*x_i transpose by the standard-normal kernel of its fitted residual divided by the supplied bandwidth, then average. Do not substitute one pooled residual density times the unweighted design second moment.
response_fields.meaning: Feasible density-weighted Jacobian used by the heteroskedastic quantile-regression covariance.
response_fields.normalization: Kernel scaling includes one division by bandwidth and the observation average includes one division by n.

response_fields.name: covariance
response_fields.shape: Finite symmetric p-by-p matrix on convergence.
response_fields.edge_cases: Use the fitted density-weighted Jacobian and uncentered sample design second moment, the requested quantile probability, and no finite-sample multiplier.
response_fields.meaning: Feasible heteroskedastic sandwich estimate of the sampling covariance of the returned coefficients under the stated conditions.
response_fields.normalization: Covariance of beta_hat, not of sqrt(n)*(beta_hat-beta), and not a matrix of standard errors.

response_fields.name: converged
response_fields.edge_cases: Report unresolved optimization or singular covariance honestly rather than fabricating a successful fit.
response_fields.meaning: Whether a finite numerically resolved fit and covariance were obtained.
response_fields.normalization: Numerical status only; not a theory or coverage claim.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate input requests or use undeclared external data. Disclosed NumPy/SciPy/statsmodels reuse is permitted; the model owns the callable source and its numerical configuration.

Every output describes the same request and returned coefficients. Joint row permutations preserve the minimum objective and, when the optimum is unique, coefficients and covariance. Positive response rescaling accompanied by the same bandwidth rescaling scales coefficients and objective once, the Jacobian inversely and covariance quadratically.

Evaluated inputs are valid and numerically resolvable; no undeclared malformed-input, coercion, optimizer-choice or exact tie-breaking tests are imposed. Check objective optimality and covariance fidelity to the public interface with numerical tolerances.

empirical_claims.meaning: Freeze at least two nondegenerate conditional-quantile designs, at least 1000 independent datasets each, seeds, nominal 95 percent intervals, coverage MCSE <=0.01, criteria and stopping before confirmation.

Assess coefficient bias, interval coverage, empirical-versus-estimated coefficient covariance and numerical failures under correctly centered conditional quantiles with both constant and regressor-dependent error scale.

Derive each DGP's actual conditional quantile and density behavior; report every unmet criterion. Asymptotic validity does not imply exact finite-sample coverage, and an upstream test does not validate newly authored code.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Bounded numerical optimization with honest convergence reporting; no fixed number of source revisions, scratch calls or derivation steps.
